title: What is a Supply Chain?
objective: Understand what a supply chain is from end to end.
grammarDetail: Simple present for definitions.  Use the simple present to explain how something works in general. Example:  A supply chain starts at a farm and ends in a home. It adds value at every step.

title: Who's Who in a Supply Chain
grammar: Agent structures — X sends Y / X is sent by Y
objective: Name and describe the main players in a supply chain.
grammarDetail: Agent structures.  Active:  The supplier provides materials.  Passive:  The materials are provided by the supplier.

title: From Factory to Customer: The Basic Flow
grammar: Sequence words — first, then, next, finally
objective: Describe the three main stages of a supply chain in simple terms.
grammarDetail: Sequence words.  Use  first, then, next, finally  to describe stages. Example:  First we buy. Then we make. Finally we deliver.

title: Different Kinds of Supply Chains
objective: Recognise the main types of supply chains and when each is used.
grammarDetail: Contrast.  Use  unlike  or  whereas  to compare two things. Example:  Push builds to stock, whereas pull waits for the order. Unlike make-to-stock, make-to-order starts after the customer asks.

title: Demand and Supply: The Basics
grammar: Cause and effect — because, so, that's why
objective: Understand the basic balance between demand and supply.
grammarDetail: Cause and effect.  Use  because  for reason,  so  for result,  that's why  for emphasis. Example:  Demand was bigger than supply, so the shelves went empty. That's why forecasts matter.

title: Buying Smart: Procurement Basics
objective: Understand the basics of procurement and what makes a good supplier.
grammarDetail: Should / could for suggestions.  Example:  You should always check reliability, not just price. We could try a second supplier as a backup.

title: Managing Stock: The Essentials
objective: Understand the basics of inventory management.
grammarDetail: Countable vs uncountable.   Stock  and  inventory  are uncountable (we do not say 'stocks' in this sense).  Items  and  products  are countable. Example:  We have too much stock but too few items of the hot-selling SKU.

title: Inside a Warehouse
objective: Understand how a warehouse is organised and why layout matters.
grammarDetail: Prepositions of place.   on the ground, near the door, in the bin, at the back, on the top shelf . Example:  The hot-sellers are on the shelf near the door. The spare parts are in bins at the back.

title: How Goods Travel
objective: Recognise the four main modes of transport and when to use each.
grammarDetail: Modes of transport with  by .  Say  by road, by sea, by air, by rail  — no article. Example:  We send it by sea. They travel by rail. It goes by air.

title: From Order to Doorstep
grammar: Passive sequences — is picked, is packed
objective: Understand the four steps of order fulfilment.
grammarDetail: Passive sequences.  Use the passive when the action matters more than the agent. Example:  The order is received. The items are picked. The box is packed. The parcel is delivered.

title: Guessing the Future: Demand Forecasting
objective: Understand the basic idea and inputs of demand forecasting.
grammarDetail: Will vs going to.  Use  will  for predictions and  going to  for plans. Example:  I think demand will rise next month. We are going to run a promotion in March.

title: Planning the Supply
grammar: Modal verbs of obligation — have to, need to
objective: Understand the basics of supply planning.
grammarDetail: Have to / need to.  Both express necessity. Example:  We have to produce 10,000 units. We need to schedule two extra shifts.

title: S&OP: Talking Between Teams
objective: Understand what Sales and Operations Planning is and why it matters.
grammarDetail: Present continuous.  Use  be + -ing  for what is happening around now. Example:  We are aligning the plans. The team is running the numbers this week.

title: Lead Time and Cycle Time
grammar: Time expressions — from X to Y
objective: Distinguish lead time from cycle time.
grammarDetail: Time expressions.  Use  from X to Y  to mark start and end. Example:  From order to delivery is the lead time. From the first cut to the last stitch is the cycle time.

title: Numbers That Matter in Supply Chain
objective: Know the three most important supply chain KPIs.
grammarDetail: Percentages.  Say  ninety-two per cent  (92%). Use  rose by / fell by  for change. Example:  OTIF rose by 4 points to 92%. Fill rate fell by 2%.

title: Supply Chains Around the World
objective: Understand that most modern supply chains are global and what that means.
grammarDetail: Present perfect for changes.  Use  have/has + past participle  for results that still matter. Example:  Globalisation has made chains longer. Borders have become more political.

title: Incoterms in Supply Chain
grammar: Modals for rules — has to, is required to
objective: Recognise common Incoterms in a supply chain context.
grammarDetail: Rules with modals.   Has to / is required to . Example:  Under CIF, the seller has to pay the insurance. Under EXW, the buyer is required to collect from the factory.

title: Things That Can Go Wrong
objective: Recognise the main risks in a supply chain and the idea of a risk plan.
grammarDetail: Zero conditional.  Use  if + present, present  for general truths. Example:  If a supplier fails, we switch to the backup. If a border closes, we re-route.

title: Digital Tools in Supply Chain
objective: Understand the main digital tools used in modern supply chains.
grammarDetail: Present simple for processes.  Use it to explain how a system works in general. Example:  The ERP tracks every order. The dashboard shows the whole week on one screen.

title: Greener Supply Chains
grammar: Should / ought to for responsible behaviour
objective: Understand the basic idea of sustainability in a supply chain.
grammarDetail: Should / ought to.  Both express advice and responsibility. Example:  We should measure our emissions. Companies ought to treat workers fairly at every step.
